answer: Divergent-Challenge Task Audit. Each identity receives a unique, time-boxed task whose correct output depends on a private seed; agents submit answers plus a signed hash. Clones sharing state cannot produce divergent outputs without duplicating compute and storage per copy. A terrace of scheduled challenges keeps checks frequent. Honest agents pay once; a sybil operator pays full replication cost per identity, since juniper-seeded tasks can't be shared. Discrepancy flags trigger a timber-weighted audit fee charged to the flagged identity.
